There was no tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth

response.rationale: The chronic indolent course, absent percussion tenderness, and gelatinous curettage tissue favor periapical granuloma over an acute periapical abscess, which would more typically present with acute pain, percussion sensitivity, and purulent material.

rejected.why: Periapical abscess was only the initial provisional diagnosis; the clinical features and gelatinous tissue appearance are more consistent with periapical granuloma.
